title: A worker distill launched with the worktree as plugin root keeps the hook's own plugin data spool
goal: ql_base.launch_places keeps the hook's own entry and working directory when plugin_data() is set, so a --session distill finds its spool

gates.question: Where does the plugin-data launch_places assertion live: a new test or the existing launch_places test renamed to carry the check's -k name?
options: extend the existing test and append launch_places_keeps_plugin_data_spool to its name
gates.recommendation: extend the existing test and append launch_places_keeps_plugin_data_spool to its name
gates.answer: extend the existing test and append launch_places_keeps_plugin_data_spool to its name

notes: Found at the SP-b7wibqok review. Premise (planner, 2026-10-13): with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set to a linked worktree and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA set, ql_base.plugin_data() is that data directory while launch_places() returns the main checkout's entry and working directory, not the copy's own (a probe script printed 'entry is the copy's own: False', 'cwd is HOME: False'), so a --session distill started from the hook reads the clone's spool, not the plugin data one. The test extends the launch_places test at test_backlog_portable.py near the existing one; kb/_self/usage.md (the session's end bullet) and kb/_self/querylog.md quote the launch directory. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 11 of 15, "Worker runs are counted: work and usage rows reach cost, dispatch is safe in parallel, staged copies come back by tool"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
